analysis:
Examined all supplied units, including unchanged validation/helpers and file metadata. ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts.swift changes compute's default from declared to current public models (head 263) and includes the artifact-selected tensor assistant in resourcePolicySHA256 (296–302). Visible worker/artifact checks remain (278–285), as do bounded strict facts decoding, duplicate-field rejection, digest validation, and qualification constraints (427–459, 482–538). No demonstrated weakening of these controls or direct change to encryption, credentials, billing, cache isolation (T-041), or privileged helper authority was found.
ClusterSetupWizardLiveOperations.swift now passes raw mtpMode and coordinator to both readAutomatic calls (head 618, 625), rather than applying discoveryMode at the caller. This enables coordinator-mode assistant planning according to the new comment, but enforcement is delegated to code outside this supplied scope; comments are not proof of enforcement. No concrete bypass is established here.
Integration must examine ClusterPublicModels.current/tensorAssistant, ClusterPlacementTensorAssistantSelection.readAutomatic/discoveryMode, and DistributedInstalledNativeStart.resourcePolicySHA256/start together: confirm coordinator mode selects only the build-declared, artifact-bound assistant; release facts and member startup compute identical assistant-inclusive policy digests; and installed assistant files, memory quotes and actual execution match that policy. These contracts matter to model/output integrity (T-007, T-012, T-027), serving availability (A-018), and qualified-build authorization (T-052/T-054); assistant execution must not be mistaken for proof of correct computation (T-056). Missing implementations and unchanged callers are coverage limits, not evidence of a regression. No supported finding in this local source scope; the delegated selection and runtime-binding contracts remain material integration questions.
